name: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
date_note: DORA already applies. Readiness is measured against an internal remediation target; set it to the date agreed with the board or supervisor.
articles_note: Article references are indicative; confirm against the supervisor's guidance.

requirements.summary: Maintain an ICT risk management framework covering identification, protection, detection, response and recovery, approved by the management body.

requirements.short: Classify and report major ICT incidents
requirements.summary: Classify ICT incidents and report major ones to the supervisor within the set deadlines.
Run a risk-based testing programme, including threat-led penetration testing where required.

requirements.short: Register of information and contract terms
requirements.summary: Keep a register of all ICT third-party arrangements and make sure contracts supporting critical functions carry the Article 30 terms, including exit plans.
ICT business continuity policy and response and recovery plans, tested regularly, with recovery time objectives for critical functions.

name: EU Payment Services Regulation (PSR)
status: Political agreement November 2025; final compromise texts April 2026; Official Journal publication expected in H2 2026 (to confirm).
date_note: Estimates. General application is 21 months after entry into force; the Verification of Payee extension (Articles 50 and 57) is 27 months after. Entry into force assumed end of 2026; adjust when the Official Journal date is known.
articles_note: Article references to be confirmed against the bank's own list of applicable articles.

sources.title: Arthur Cox, final compromise texts published
Sopra Steria, PSR in 2026: state of play for banks
Taylor Wessing, EU lawmakers strike a deal

requirements.short: Verification of Payee for all credit transfers
requirements.summary: Check that the payee name matches the IBAN for all credit transfers, free of charge and within seconds, and warn the payer before authorisation. Strict liability for losses caused by a failed check. Non-consumers may opt out for bulk channels.
Monitor transactions before execution, in real time for instant credit transfers. Failure to monitor shifts fraud losses to the bank.

requirements.short: Payee-side monitoring before funds are made available
requirements.summary: Monitor incoming payments before crediting the payee, including instant payments, to stop mule accounts receiving fraud proceeds.

Refund consumers deceived by someone impersonating the bank, once they report it to the police and the bank. Decide within 15 business days. The bank carries the burden of proof; SCA alone is not proof of gross negligence.
Refund unauthorised transactions by the end of the next business day unless fraud is suspected and reported. Consumer liability capped at EUR 50, zero where SCA was not applied.
Maintain technical safeguards against replication of the bank's phone numbers, domains and email addresses, and cooperate with telecoms and online platforms to remove fraudulent content.
Report fraud data to the competent authority in the harmonised EBA format. Optional fraud-signal sharing with other PSPs needs a joint DPIA and cannot be the sole basis for de-risking decisions.
Apply SCA to online account access, payment initiation and any remote action with fraud risk, such as changing contact details, creating payment tokens and changing spending limits.
Offer more than one means of SCA and at least one that does not depend on a smartphone, for people with disabilities, older people and those with low digital skills.
Activate a new mobile app instance only with SCA and a separate channel, with a default four-hour delay the customer can adjust.

Provide a dedicated API with the same data and response times as customer channels, publish quarterly availability and performance statistics, run a testing facility for TPPs, and remove prohibited obstacles. Screen scraping is no longer a fallback.
Give customers a neutral dashboard in the app and online banking to see, withdraw and re-establish open banking access, with purpose, data categories and access dates.
Disclose currency conversion mark-ups before the transaction, as an amount and as a percentage over the ECB reference rate. No value dating to the customer's detriment.
Show ATM charges before the withdrawal and treat cardholders of other PSPs equally. Supports cash without purchase at retailers.
Let customers set and change spending limits and block payment types or channels, under SCA.

requirements.short: Complaints within 15 business days and ADR information
requirements.summary: Respond to payment complaints within 15 business days (35 in exceptional cases) and show ADR details prominently on the website, app, in branches and in terms and conditions.
Update terms and conditions, pre-contract information and customer communications for new liability, refund, SCA and transparency rules.

requirements.short: Fraud awareness for customers and staff
requirements.summary: Run regular fraud awareness campaigns and staff training on current fraud types.
Put outsourcing agreements in place where digital wallet operators verify SCA elements. The bank stays fully liable for SCA failures by the wallet operator.
Map PSR obligations to controls and owners, evidence compliance, and prepare for higher harmonised penalties and possible personal accountability of management.

name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
status: In force since August 2024. Stand-alone high-risk obligations moved to 2 December 2027 under the 2026 provisional agreement (to confirm).
date_note: Dates follow the 2026 digital omnibus agreement; confirm the final adopted text.
articles_note: AI used to evaluate creditworthiness or establish credit scores of natural persons is listed as high-risk.

sources.title: Sidley: provisional agreement to delay key EU AI Act obligations

requirements.short: AI system inventory and risk classification
requirements.summary: Keep an inventory of AI systems and classify each by risk category.

requirements.short: Risk management and human oversight for high-risk AI
requirements.summary: For high-risk uses such as credit scoring of individuals, run risk management, data governance, logging and human oversight.
Tell customers when they interact with an AI system such as a chatbot.
